description: Bank statement descriptor patterns, matched in order. This file says what the document SAYS — a movement type and a counterparty name. It deliberately says nothing about which channel a credit belongs to or whether it is in scope: those are reconciliation conclusions, and letting ingestion decide them would make the confidence score circular. See ADR-0002.
lesson: Wompi changed its own descriptor mid-period, from 'PAGO DE PROV WOMPI S.A.S.' to 'PAGO DE TERC WOMPI S.A.S.' on 2026-04-14. A rule pinned to the first spelling silently dropped every settlement after that date. Rules now capture the counterparty from whatever follows the service prefix, so a new payer — or the same payer under a new prefix — is recognised rather than lost.

rules.note: The supplier-payment service, seen from our side: the named party is paying us.

scope: Only the two inflow prefixes a payer uses to pay us are classified. The challenge is Wompi → Bancolombia → Odoo, and bank charges, VAT, interest, payroll and PSE debits are out of it: they fall to the fallback as OTHER, which has no account, so no entry is ever proposed for them. The two prefixes stay generic rather than pinned to 'WOMPI' on purpose — see 'lesson'. A non-Wompi payer is still named, and the ERP reconciliation refuses to propose an entry for money that did not come through a connected channel.
